faq.a: College athletic directors, senior associate ADs, and administrators at institutions that have no rugby program today and are weighing whether to introduce it as a varsity sport.

faq.q: Does our college need a rugby club first?
faq.a: No. This is about starting a brand-new varsity program from the ground up. No existing club, field, or history is required — just a decision to build one.

faq.q: Is travel included in the budget?
faq.a: Yes. The example budget includes travel and competition for both squads across a regional, drivable schedule. Every college's travel cost differs with its location and opponents.

faq.q: Are the dollar figures real quotes?
faq.a: No. The budget is an illustrative example of the shape of a first-year program — mostly people, very little capital. Every college should replace it with its own net-tuition and cost figures.
Many programs launch both squads at once: one head coach, one equipment budget, and one travel schedule can cover two rosters, and the marginal cost of the second squad is small.
In a collegiate rugby league with small-college divisions, typically fall 15s and spring 7s against regional opponents.

faq.q: What if the roster doesn't fill?
faq.a: The exploratory phase ends with a defined go/no-go gate. If verified commitments don't reach the roster floor by the agreed date, the launch simply moves to the next year at no sunk cost beyond the coach search.
